verses.text: During David's reign there was a famine for three years in a row. David went to the LORD for an answer. The LORD said, “This is because of Saul and his bloodstained family. He put the Gibeonites to death.”

The king called the Gibeonites in to speak to them. They weren't Israelites but survivors of the Amorites. Israel had sworn to spare them, but Saul in his zeal for Israel and Judah had tried to kill them.
David asked the Gibeonites, “What can I do for you? How can I make things right so that you'll bless the people who belong to the LORD?”
They told him, “This isn't about money owed to us by Saul or his family. And we have no right to put anyone in Israel to death.” David said, “Tell me what you want me to do, and I'll do it.”
They answered the king, “There was a man who cut us down and plotted to wipe us out, so we'd have no place anywhere in Israel.
Hand over seven of his male descendants to us. We'll hang them before the LORD at Gibeah, the town of Saul, whom the LORD chose.” The king said, “I'll hand them over.”
But the king spared Mephibosheth son of Jonathan and grandson of Saul because of the oath David and Saul's son Jonathan had made to each other before the LORD.

Instead the king took Armoni and Mephibosheth, the two sons Rizpah daughter of Aiah had borne to Saul. He also took the five sons Saul's daughter Merab had borne to Adriel son of Barzillai from Meholah.

He handed them over to the Gibeonites, who hanged them on the mountain before the LORD. All seven died together. They were put to death in the first days of harvest, when the barley harvest was just beginning.

Rizpah daughter of Aiah spread sackcloth out on the rock for herself. From the start of harvest until rain poured down on the bodies, she kept the birds away by day and the wild animals away by night.
David heard what Rizpah daughter of Aiah, Saul's concubine, had done.

David went to get the bones of Saul and his son Jonathan from the people of Jabesh Gilead. They had stolen the bodies from the street in Beth Shan, where the Philistines had hung them after killing Saul at Gilboa.
David brought back the bones of Saul and his son Jonathan, and they gathered up the bones of the seven who had been hanged.
They buried Saul and Jonathan's bones in Zela, in the land of Benjamin, in the tomb of Saul's father Kish. They did everything the king commanded. After that, God answered prayer for the land.
The Philistines went to war with Israel again. David and his men went down and fought them, and David grew exhausted.
Ishbibenob was a descendant of the giant. His bronze spearhead weighed three hundred shekels, and he was armed with a new sword. He intended to kill David.
But Abishai son of Zeruiah came to David's aid and killed the Philistine. Then David's men swore to him, “You can't go into battle with us again. We can't let the lamp of Israel go out.”
Later there was another battle with the Philistines at Gob. Sibbecai the Hushathite killed Saph, another descendant of the giant.
In another battle with the Philistines at Gob, Elhanan son of Jaare-Oregim from Bethlehem killed the brother of Goliath from Gath. The shaft of his spear was as thick as a weaver's beam.
There was another battle at Gath. A huge man there had six fingers on each hand and six toes on each foot, twenty-four altogether. He too was a descendant of the giant.
He defied Israel, and Jonathan, the son of David's brother Shimei, killed him.
These four were descendants of the giant in Gath. They fell at the hands of David and his men.
